My name is Leslie Anderson. I'm the Director of Planning and Development for the City of Saskatoon.
The report before you tonight outlines a recommendation for the city and to enter into a lease agreement with Greater Saskatoon Catholic schools.
For a portion of a municipal reserve within the Grace Adam Metaway-Winnick Park at 1510-19th Street West.
The purpose of the lease is to support student safety at St. Mary's Wellness and Education Center by creating a secure outdoor area on the land immediately west of the school.
The item is before you tonight as it requires public notice for the lease of the dedicated lands.
In recent years, the school has identified increasing safety concerns on and around the school grounds,
including discarded hazardous materials and behaviors not compatible with the safe learning environment.
In the fall of 2025, the school invited a number of members of administration and other organizations including a couple of counselors out for a site visit
to share what they were experiencing.
And also in the fall of the school board undertook community consultation about what should be done in the surrounding area.
And that feedback that they receive from the community confirmed the need for enhanced student safety and secure outdoor space.
So in late November, the school board formally requested a long-term lease of the municipal reserve to allow them to fence the area and to provide for safety improvements for the students.
We definitely recognize that this request is a typical to allow the fencing of municipal reserve lands and the exclusive use of the space by the school.
But it is being brought forward due to the extenuating circumstances present in the immediate area.
So the lease would include a proposed area of 1.061 acres of municipal reserve located within the park.
The school board will be responsible for the ongoing maintenance and operational costs of that fence area.
The city would be responsible for ongoing maintenance around that site.
So outside the fence area.
The school board will be responsible for the irrigation and other operations within the fence.
We do estimate that the city will be responsible for a removal of a small hill that exists in the park.
And that's estimated to cost approximately $8,000.
That would be covered by the park enhancement fund, which is a reserve that funds changes such as this and is accommodated in this year's work plan for that fund.
So the school board is responsible for a number of costs related to this, but we are responsible for that small hill and re-turfing the area.
The property will remain tax exempt, which is consistent with its current use.
So should council approve the lease.
We would then proceed with implementation based on the terms outlined in the report and the subsequent agreement.
And the school board anticipates to move forward with fencing of the site in the near future early this year.
